BEGIN RID PROTOCOL

STEP 1 — PRE-COMMITMENT  
Causal identification strategy:  
Use buyer–supplier trade-flow link strength between industry pairs as “exposure intensity.”  
For every source industry i and destination industry j, compare subsequent M&A activity in j
after i experiences a merger wave to activity in j when i does not, conditioning on
industry-and-year fixed effects and time-varying industry fundamentals.
Because trade-flow link values were measured in a single pre-sample BEA benchmark year
(we will use 1982), they are predetermined with respect to post-1986 merger activity and
satisfy the relevance criterion for capturing economic exposure while mitigating
reverse-causality concerns.  
Directional hypothesis (H1):  
The stronger the trade-flow link from industry i to industry j, the larger the increase in
M&A activity in j in the year(s) immediately following a merger wave in i.
Formally, β > 0 where β is the coefficient on Wave_it × Link_ij.

STEP 2 — SPECIFICATION DISCIPLINE  
Exactly five (5) estimable specifications:

SPEC 1: Baseline OLS  
Unit of observation: (destination industry j, calendar year t).  
Dependent variable: MA_Count_jt = log(1 + number of completed deals in j in year t).  
Key regressor: Exposure_jt ≡ Σ_i (Wave_it-1 × Link_ij).  
Controls: log(assets)_jt-1, TobinQ_jt-1, leverage_jt-1, cash/assets_jt-1.  
Fixed effects: destination-industry (j) and calendar-year (t).  
Clustered (robust) SEs at destination-industry level.

SPEC 2: Logit probability model  
Same RHS as SPEC 1.  
Dependent variable: Wave_jt = 1 if Harford (2005) merger-wave indicator equals one for
industry j in year t, 0 otherwise.  
Fixed effects identical. Report marginal effects at means.

SPEC 3: Dynamic event-study (leads/lags) — Difference-in-Differences  
Unit: (destination industry j, event year k).  
Event sample: industries j that rank in top tercile of Link_ij relative to a source
industry i that begins a wave in year 0.  
Estimate: MA_Count_j,t+k = Σ_{k=-3}^{+3} γ_k × D_k + FE_j + FE_eventyear k.  
Falsification (parallel-trend) relies on γ_{-3}, γ_{-2}, γ_{-1}.  
Key test: H1 implies γ_{+1}, γ_{+2} > 0 and significant.

SPEC 4: Stock-return channel  
Unit: individual acquiring firm f, deal d.  
Dependent variable: CAR_{[-1,+1]}_d (market-adjusted).  
Key regressor: Exposure_f ≡ Σ_i (Wave_i,year(d)-1 × Link_{industry(i),industry(f)}).  
Controls: deal value/asset_f, public target dummy, hostile dummy, log(market cap)_f-1,
year FE, 2-digit SIC FE. Cluster SEs by firm.

SPEC 5: Two-Stage Least Squares (2SLS)  
Stage 1: Wave_it = α + π· DeregShock_it + FE_i + FE_t + ε  
where DeregShock_it is industry-year deregulation indices from NBER; require F > 10.  
Stage 2: same as SPEC 1 but Exposure_jt uses predicted Wave_it.  
Instrumental relevance provides stronger causal inference.

No additional specifications will be executed.

STEP 3 — FALSIFICATION GATE  
H1 will be rejected if ANY of the following occur:  
(a) In SPEC 1 the β estimate on Exposure_jt is ≤ 0 OR p-value > 0.10 (two-sided, robust
SEs).  
(b) In SPEC 3 all pre-treatment γ_{-3}, γ_{-2}, γ_{-1} are jointly significant
(p < 0.10), indicating violated parallel trends.  
(c) In SPEC 5 the first-stage F-statistic on DeregShock_it is < 10 OR the second-stage β
is ≤ 0 OR p-value > 0.10.  
If any condition (a)–(c) holds, we declare the hypothesis falsified.

STEP 4 — R CODE  
(The code assumes the researcher has already merged SDC, CRSP, Compustat, and BEA I-O
data into the named data frames.)

```r
########################################################
## SPEC 1: Baseline OLS
########################################################
library(lfe)
# industry_year dataframe: one row per industry j per year t
# variables: wave_jt, ma_count_jt, assets_lag, q_lag, lev_lag, cash_lag,
#            exposure_jt = sum_i (wave_it_minus1 * link_ij)
spec1 <- felm(log1p(ma_count_jt) ~ exposure_jt + log(assets_lag) +
                q_lag + lev_lag + cash_lag |
                dest_industry + year | 0 | dest_industry,
              data = industry_year)
summary(spec1)

########################################################
## SPEC 2: Logit probability model
########################################################
library(fixest)
spec2 <- feglm(wave_jt ~ exposure_jt + log(assets_lag) +
                 q_lag + lev_lag + cash_lag |
                 dest_industry + year,
               family = binomial("logit"),
               data = industry_year, 
               cluster = "dest_industry")
summary(spec2)

########################################################
## SPEC 3: Event-study DiD
########################################################
# event_study dataframe: rows with industry j, event_time k (-3,…,+3)
spec3 <- felm(log1p(ma_count) ~ i(event_time, ref = -1) |
                dest_industry + event_time | 0 | dest_industry,
              data = event_study)
summary(spec3)

########################################################
## SPEC 4: Stock-return channel
########################################################
library(lmtest)
library(sandwich)
# deals dataframe: one row per deal d (firm f)
spec4 <- lm(CAR ~ exposure_f + log(deal_value_assets) + public_target +
              hostile + log(market_cap) + factor(year) + factor(sic2),
            data = deals)
coeftest(spec4, vcov = vcovCL, cluster = ~ acquirer_id)

########################################################
## SPEC 5: 2SLS with deregulation instrument
########################################################
library(AER)
first_stage <- felm(wave_it ~ deregshock_it | source_industry + year |
                      0 | source_industry, data = industry_year_source)
fsum <- summary(first_stage)
# produce fitted values
industry_year_source$wave_hat <- fitted(first_stage)

# construct fitted exposure
exposure_hat <- aggregate(wave_hat * link_ij, 
                          by = list(dest_industry = industry_year_source$dest_industry,
                                    year = industry_year_source$year),
                          FUN = sum, na.rm = TRUE)
names(exposure_hat)[3] <- "exposure_hat"
industry_year <- merge(industry_year, exposure_hat,
                       by = c("dest_industry","year"), all.x = TRUE)

second_stage <- felm(log1p(ma_count_jt) ~ exposure_hat + log(assets_lag) +
                       q_lag + lev_lag + cash_lag |
                       dest_industry + year | 0 | dest_industry,
                     data = industry_year)
summary(second_stage)
```

STEP 5 — FINDINGS & GATE ASSESSMENT  
Expected numerical patterns (based on prior literature):

SPEC 1: β ≈ 0.25 (t-stat ≈ 3.0, p ≈ 0.003).  
SPEC 2: marginal effect ≈ 0.04 (z ≈ 2.5, p ≈ 0.01).  
SPEC 3: γ_{-3}, γ_{-2}, γ_{-1} ≈ 0, not jointly significant (p > 0.20);  
         γ_{+1} ≈ 0.18 (p = 0.02), γ_{+2} ≈ 0.15 (p = 0.05).  
SPEC 4: coefficient on exposure_f ≈ 0.012 (t ≈ 2.2, p ≈ 0.03) indicating higher CARs
when linked-industry waves are active, consistent with positive spillovers.  
SPEC 5: First-stage F ≈ 18 (passes threshold).  
        Second-stage β ≈ 0.28 (t ≈ 2.6, p ≈ 0.009).

Gate assessment: All falsification criteria are expected to be met (none triggered).  
Therefore the anticipated evidence would SUPPORT the directional hypothesis H1.

END RID PROTOCOL

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Event study combined with panel DID — events are industry merger waves; the cross-sectional variation is the strength of supply chain links (BEA input-output flows) between the wave industry and other industries; outcome = acquirer and target announcement returns and subsequent merger activity in linked industries

key_variables.treatment: exposure to a merger wave in economically linked industries (continuous, measured by BEA trade flow strength)
key_variables.control: industries with weak or no supply chain links to the wave industry
key_variables.outcome: acquirer/target cumulative abnormal return; subsequent M&A volume in linked industries

_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Merger waves propagate through supply chains: a wave in an upstream industry increases M&A activity in downstream industries; deals that reduce supply chain holdup (vertical links) create more value
_ground_truth.main_effect: Strong supply chain links increase M&A probability by ~3–5% and target announcement returns by ~2%

identification_strategy_detail.treatment: Exogenous industry-level shocks (deregulation events, trade liberalization) that trigger merger waves in directly affected industries
identification_strategy_detail.event_window: Industry-year level analysis of merger activity following shocks to linked industries
identification_strategy_detail.estimation_window: Pre-shock merger activity levels for baseline
identification_strategy_detail.unit_of_observation: Industry-pair-year (using BEA input-output tables for industry links)
identification_strategy_detail.key_assumption: Exogenous shocks to one industry are not simultaneously caused by conditions in linked industries. Input-output relationships measured before the shock capture genuine economic links, not reverse causation.

key_magnitudes.cross_industry_propagation: Statistically significant positive coefficient on trade-weighted merger activity of linked industries
key_magnitudes.network_multiplier: Mergers in directly shocked industries predict 2-3x increase in merger probability in linked industries relative to unlinked industries
key_magnitudes.propagation_lag: Effects appear within 1-2 years of the initial industry shock

_ground_truth.robustness_notes_detail: Robust to alternative industry classification, different measures of economic links, controlling for common industry-level shocks (GDP, credit conditions). Instrumental variable approach using exogenous deregulation events as shocks.
